Pakistani cricketers’ phones confiscated in England. Suspicion of match-fixing is the reason

The mobile phones were reportedly taken into PCB custody after Pakistan’s defeat in second Test against England, with data from the devices transferred before players returned home.

Debdutta Chakraborty

07 September, 2026 08:18 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Pakistan's Imam-ul-Haq reacts after being dimissed by England pacer Jofra Archer | Lee Smith | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Pakistan’s England T our is getting murkier by the day. First, they considered not allowing players to return to the field at Lord’s after Sky News broadcast an interview with jailed former PM Imran Khan’s sons. Second, they fired seven players and the team’s head coach after the series loss. N ow they’ve confiscated the players’ phones on suspicions of match-fixing. It’s a never-ending loop of trouble and turmoil for the team.

Over the weekend, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) launched an internal inquiry into player discipline following media reports concerning the activities of batters Imam-ul-Haq and Mohammad Rizwan during the team’s England tour. Their mobile phones were reportedly taken into PCB custody after Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test, with data from the devices transferred before the players returned home, reportedly as part of routine procedures.

PCB Director of Media and Digital Communications Amir Mir confirmed that the board was reviewing the matter, urging the public to rely on official statements rather than unverified reports circulating from external sources.

Show Full Article

“The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally. The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration,” Mir wrote on X.

According to Pakistani outlet 365 News , the phones will reportedly remain with the PCB until the third and final Test at Edgbaston, which begins on 9 September.

The investigation comes after major changes to Pakistan’s squad and coaching setup following their 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s, a result that gave England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.

The PCB released Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Imam-ul-Haq, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad, Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Zafar from the squad. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also sent home, with Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke brought in as their replacements.

Seven additional players were subsequently added to the squad for the Edgbaston Test. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience, while Arafat Minhas, Saad Baig, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Junior are yet to make their Test debuts. Minhas, however, has already represented Pakistan in ODIs and T20Is.

Also read: Coke Studio’s Gen Z reboot Nu.WAV divides Pakistanis. ‘Give us back the old version’

‘Worst cricket board’ Pakistanis cannot take the downfall of cricket in their country anymore.

“Mobile phones of players in PCB custody This is quite unbelievable. What is our cricket board Upto ? Surely the worst cricket board in last 70 years of our existence,” former Sindh governor Mohammad Zubair wrote on X.

Given the joke it has become, a parody account on X added: “PCB has won more controversies than matches in this series”.

Former cricketer Tanveer called it a ‘shameful act’ symbolic of the fact that something of this scale has never occurred before.

Meanwhile, former cricketers Misbah-ul-Haq and Shoaib Akhtar have also spoken up. Akhtar said the Pakistan Cricket Board has lost faith in the current squad and is increasingly looking toward a younger generation of players.

Haq questioned the country’s broader cricketing structure and criticised what he sees as unequal treatment of local and foreign coaches, calling on the board to adopt a long-term strategy rather than repeatedly making decisions in response to short-term setbacks.

Speaking on the “OutSide EDGE” programme, Akhtar suggested that the PCB’s plans go beyond simply responding to Pakistan’s disappointing Test series in England. According to him, the board is preparing for a significant overhaul of the national team.

In the show, he also recalled a conversation with a PCB official who, according to Akhtar, indicated that the board’s expectations now rested primarily with the next generation of players being prepared for international cricket. Haq, however, called for patience, proper evaluation and a coherent long-term plan.

Pakistanis have no hope left. They have moved on from even blaming Mohsin Naqvi anymore.

“I am done blaming Mohsin Naqvi for PCB’s screw ups. The buck does NOT stop at Naqvi; it stops with the Patron-in-Chief of the PCB who is the PM of Pakistan @CMShehbaz. Sir, something is awfully broken and it is on you to now fix it. Hybrid or not, you need to exercise your powers. We need a dedicated PCB Chairman and not a bits-and-pieces part-timer. Yes, that may not fix everything, but start tackling the problem one thing at a time, please!”, Pakistani cricket commentator Shahab wrote on X .

(Edited by Saptak Datta)

India needs double-digit factory growth to meet its goals for manufacturing sector—Bank of America report

Expanding manufacturing is seen as crucial to moving more workers from farms into better-paying jobs. It’s also seen as critical for PM Modi’s ‘Viksit Bharat’ ambition.

Ruchi Bhatia

07 September, 2026 05:17 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

An electric vehicle assembly line in India. | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

India will need to sharply accelerate manufacturing growth to meet its long-standing ambitions for the sector, according to Bank of America economists, who point to several constraints holding the country back from becoming a factory hub for the world.

BofA economists led by Rahul Bajoria estimate that India’s manufacturing sector will need to expand at an annual pace of at least 10% over the next 15 years to lift its share of the economy to 25%. That assumes overall gross domestic product growth of about 7% a year.

At that pace, India’s manufacturing sector could expand to almost $2.3 trillion by 2040, from about $500 billion in 2024, while its share of global manufacturing would more than double to 6.3%, they wrote in a research note Monday

Show Full Article

India’s economic trajectory has been unusual compared with many other developed nations. Services became the main growth engine before manufacturing developed into a major source of jobs, leaving a large share of the population still dependent on agriculture. Expanding manufacturing is seen as crucial to moving more workers from farms into better-paying jobs.

It’s also seen as critical Narendra Modi’s ‘Viksit Bharat’ ambition of turning India into a developed economy by 2047.

Modi has expressed confidence in India’s ability to reach the goal. Latest figures showed India’s economy expanded at a brisk 7.8% pace in the three months through June from a year earlier, beating expectations, with manufacturing growing 9.2%. In a celebratory tweet, Modi described the outcome as a “herculean feat.”

In its note on Monday, Bofa said India “perceivably punches below its weight” given its resources and workforce, while warning that “without substantially growing its manufacturing sector for both domestic consumption and exports, the prospects of Viksit Bharat by 2047 will be diminished.”

India has rolled out more than $26 billion of incentives over the past decade to attract manufacturers and build domestic supply chains. The push has helped draw companies including Apple Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co., and fueled a surge in iPhone production and exports.

Yet, “India’s manufacturing sector has broadly stagnated in its GDP share,” BofA said, at about 17%.

BofA identified regulatory burdens and high power costs as key constraints. India has 92.6 million micro enterprises but only about 40,000 medium-sized firms, a disparity that weighs on productivity and the creation of quality jobs.

Manufacturing MSMEs can face as many as 1,400 compliance obligations a year, making it harder for smaller firms to grow, they said. Industrial users also pay 10%-25% above the cost of electricity supply, compared with about 10% below cost in Vietnam.

Novo Nordisk stops 2 more trials for its heart disease medicine in fresh setback

Earlier this year, Novo said ziltivekimab failed to reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes, diminishing expectations for other ongoing studies.

Ashleigh Furlong

07 September, 2026 05:12 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

The Novo Nordisk A/S logo during a news conference in Mumbai, India, on Tuesday, June 24, 2025. Novo Nordisk said it will sell its blockbuster weight-loss treatment Wegovy in India starting at $50 a week, tailoring the price to match the pocket of consumers in a nation with the worlds third-largest obese population. | Dhiraj Singh/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Novo Nordisk A/S stopped two more trials for its experimental heart disease medicine, in a further blow to the drug’s prospects.

Earlier this year, Novo said ziltivekimab failed to reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes, diminishing expectations for other ongoing studies.

The Danish drugmaker said Monday it halted two trials testing whether ziltivekimab would help patients with heart failure, each looking at different outcomes.

Show Full Article

Novo shares slipped 0.6% in Copenhagen. They are down about 10% since the drugmaker reported the failure of the ziltivekimab trial in late July.

The data monitoring committee found a “low likelihood of a different outcome” in the two trials to the previous study failure, a Novo spokesperson said. The pharmaceutical news site Endpoints first reported Novo’s move.

It comes after Novartis reported its experimental heart drug also failed to help reduce deaths, heart attacks and strokes, casting doubt on the theory that underpinned research on the medicine.

Novo will continue a different study looking at the potential benefit of ziltivekimab following a heart attack, the spokesperson said.
